subject: DSR triage: identity verification, retention hold, and controller/processor decision
messages:
From: Alex Johnson <privacy@acme-corp.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Complete deletion + access copy for user ID 58f9c2

Hi Vanessa,

We are submitting a formal Data Subject Request under the GDPR for one of our users (internal ID: 58f9c2). They are requesting:
- A complete export of all personal data you hold about them (including embeddings, logs, and any derived tokens)
- Full deletion from your production systems and backups where feasible

Attached is the signed DSR form and a token list we were provided to help match records. Please confirm the identity verification steps you need and an estimated timeline for export and deletion. Also flag whether Redwood considers Acme Corp the controller or processor for this interaction — our security team needs that on record.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Privacy Lead, Acme Corp
privacy@acme-corp.com

Attachment: acme_dsr_request_20270822.pdf (application/pdf, 42 KB)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <privacy@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Complete deletion + access copy for user ID 58f9c2

Hi Alex — thanks for the submission and the signed form. We're starting triage. Quick summary of next steps we recommend and the info we need from Acme to proceed: 

1) Identity verification: please confirm the following (we can accept via your legal-ops email):
   - The account email or hashed identifier used on your side for user 58f9c2
   - A signed POA if this is being submitted by a representative (signed by the account owner)

2) Scope clarification: you asked for "all personal data" — do you want:
   a) All interaction logs (API request/response payloads) including prompt text and model outputs?
   b) Embedding vectors and associated metadata?
   c) Any archived backups older than 90 days (note: restores from deep backups may take longer and have legal constraints)?

3) Controller vs Processor: our standard posture is that Acme (the customer) is the controller for their end users and Redwood is a processor for customer data processed on the Redwood service. If you believe Acme needs Redwood to take on controller responsibilities for any part of this request, please outline which processing activities you intend Redwood to control so we can escalate internally.

Technical notes for Acme and internal engineering:
- Export: We can provide a machine-readable archive (JSONL) that includes timestamps, interaction metadata, and the non-aggregated tokens associated with the account. Large exports will be delivered via a secure signed URL (we typically use a 7-day expiry).
- Deletion: Deletion is performed at multiple tiers — active index, object store (S3), and cache. We will remove primary objects and then kick off a background sweep for derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes). Deletions from immutable backups require: (1) a backup retention exception or (2) an on-request retention purge if allowed by contract and regulatory constraints.

I've looped in Dev for an engineering estimate on timelines and Marissa from privacy to advise on the controller/processor framing and any contractual steps (e.g., Data Processing Amendment addendum). Dev / Marissa — can you confirm the expected timing if Acme confirms identity and scope today?

Regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <privacy@acme-corp.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Complete deletion + access copy for user ID 58f9c2

Vanessa / Marissa — quick engineering breakdown and ETA assumptions if Acme supplies the identity tokens and confirms scope (a/b/c from Vanessa):

- Export: small export (~150MB) for a single user: 1 business day to prepare, scan logs, and stage encrypted archive. We will scrub keys and return a signed URL for download.
- Deletion (active systems): 24-48 hours to remove primary objects and purge caches (prefix and KV caches).
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, vector index entries): estimate 3-7 days depending on index compaction cycles; we run compaction nightly but full index rebuilds can be required for thorough removal.
- Backups/archives: if Acme wants us to remove copies from immutable backups we need a contractual retention exception — otherwise removal occurs at the next retention cycle (typically 90 days). If customer provides legal justification/POA we can open an expedited backup purge request but this requires SOC 2 log review and infra tickets which add 5-10 business days.

Notes on evidence: Acme asked for proof of deletion. We can provide:
- Export bundle (JSONL) as proof of data delivered.
- Internal deletion runbook excerpt and timestamped deletion job logs (redacted system identifiers).
- For backups, we can provide a written attestation and the ticket numbers for the backup purge request when executed.

Action items:
- Acme: confirm scope (a/b/c) + signed POA / identity confirmation.
- Redwood (Eng): upon confirmation we will open REDWOOD-3145 and REDWOOD-3146 for export and deletion; estimated completion 1–10 business days depending on options selected.

Dev
Staff Software Engineer, Platform
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Johnson <privacy@acme-corp.com>, Legal Ops <legal-ops@acme-corp.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Complete deletion + access copy for user ID 58f9c2

Thanks Vanessa & Dev — a few privacy/legal points to ensure we stay compliant and minimize risk: 

1) Controller/Processor confirmation: I'll send a short DPA addendum template to Alex that clarifies Acme is the controller for their end users and Redwood continues as processor. If Acme requires Redwood to assume controller responsibilities for any subset, we need explicit written acceptance and legal review — that will push timelines.

2) Identity proof: acceptable forms are (a) email confirmation from account owner to privacy@acme-corp.com, or (b) the signed POA attached. Alex — please confirm which you will provide.

3) Escalation & regulatory timelines: we will treat this as an urgent DSR. If the export/deletion cannot be completed within 30 days due to backup constraints or technical complexity, we will: 
   - Provide an interim access export and a detailed remediation timeline, and
   - Offer a written attestation of the deletion operations completed to date.

4) Evidence package: we will include the export bundle, deletion job logs (timestamps), and an attestation letter signed by Redwood Legal. Please note the attestation will not include raw system identifiers for customer security reasons; we will include ticket IDs and hashed run ids.

Planned deliverables once Acme confirms:
- Day 1: Identity confirmation + scope signed off
- Day 1–2: Export bundle prepared and shared via secure link
- Day 1–7: Active system deletion + cache purge
- Day 3–10: Index compaction and derived artifact removal (if selected)
- If backup purge requested and approved: additional 5–10 business days and written attestation

Alex — we'll wait for the POA or email confirmation before kicking off REDWOOD-3145/3146.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Privacy Counsel, Redwood Inference

Please proceed with the export first; we will await the secure link and the deletion ETA for active systems. If we decide later to request backup purges we'll re-open the conversation with legal justification.

Alex
